definition: The Weidner Multi-Lingual Word Processing System was a computer-assisted translation technology released in the United States in 1977 by Weidner Communications Corporation (WCC), a now defunct US company.
details: The system represented a significant breakthrough in machine translation and multilingual word processing, improving translation efficiency and output for commercial applications.

explainer.lead: The Weidner Multi-Lingual Word Processing System was a computer-assisted translation technology released in the United States in 1977 by Weidner Communications Corporation. It mattered as a commercial breakthrough for machine translation and multilingual word processing.

tiers.eli5: It was an early computer tool from the 1970s that helped people translate and edit documents in more than one language.
tiers.practitioner: It is now a historical system; its relevance to engineers is as a reference point for how translation tooling was commercialised before modern neural methods. The pitfall is expecting modern capability from it: it was computer-assisted translation, not autonomous translation.
tiers.paperLevel: It is described as a computer-assisted translation and multilingual word-processing system released in 1977 by a now-defunct US company. Its documented contribution is improved translation efficiency and output for commercial applications.

explainer.example: A 1970s company needing documents in several languages could use the system to assist translators and produce consistent output faster than manual drafting.
